topics.topic: Startup ownership between service_entry and run_service, including who creates and passes the app dependencies
questions: Which returned values and clock function are passed to `create_app`, and does `run_service` itself own all four startup steps or receive the already-created surface described by `flow:service_start`?

Does `run_service` own the complete startup sequence, or does `boundary:service_entry` call those three operations before invoking `run_service` only to serve the already-built surface, as `flow:service_start` states?

quotes: Calls `public_op:deliverer_api.load_config`, `public_op:deliverer_api.read_token` and `public_op:deliverer_api.create_app` in that order, then serves the surface on the loopback interface until it is stopped.
`capability:deliverer_api.run_service` runs that surface in the web server, on the loopback interface.
judgement.divergence: One implementation makes `run_service` load configuration, read the token and create the app itself; another has the service-entry boundary perform those operations once and passes the resulting surface to `run_service`, which the deployment process and health checker notice when a startup input changes between the two possible reads.
judgement.why: State 5 makes `run_service` the owner of initialization, while the accepted startup flow makes it a serving operation applied to the surface already built in the preceding step.
